subject: Halo4B elevated 502s — incident notice and recovery update
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@acme.com>, platform-alerts@acme.com
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Halo4B elevated 502s — initial notice

Hi Maya + Acme platform team,

We’re seeing a spike in 502 (Bad Gateway) responses originating from the Halo4B model serving pool that began at ~08:40 PST this morning. The spike is concentrated on streaming/generation requests with longer context (>1,024 tokens) and appears as partial responses followed by a 502 rather than a soft 4xx.

Impact:
- ~6–8% error rate on Halo4B-rw endpoints for Acme’s org key between 08:40–09:00 PST.
- Short-lived but visible failures for streaming calls; retries are mostly successful when routed to the fallback model.

What we’ve done so far (mitigations in place):
- Enabled automatic fallback to a pinned compatible variant (halo4b-stable-quant) for affected routes.
- Temporarily increased instance count for Halo4B pool and disabled a recent kernel optimization rollout for Halo4B.
- Applied a short-term prefix caching rule for Acme traffic to reduce hot-spot KV pressure.

Attachments: sample request IDs and truncated error samples attached (halo4b-error-samples.txt, request-ids.csv).

Next steps: our SRE lead (cc’d) is triaging and will follow up with a technical update within 2–4 hours. I’ll also provide an ETA for full recovery as soon as we have root-cause confidence.

We understand the impact this has on your end-to-end experience and apologize for the disruption — we’re treating this as a high-priority incident.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Vanessa / Hannah — quick triage notes and recommended customer text:

What we see (prelim):
- Error mode: 502 during streaming completion, often after ~1.2s of token generation.
- Root trigger: correlated with a kernel selection path introduced in rollout v1.3.2 for Halo4B; the kernel incorrectly handles KV cache pointer updates during certain sequence-length boundary conditions. That causes a transient segmentation in the runtime that surfaces as a failed gRPC stream (502).
- Repro: internal test harness reproduces at ~80% probability with synthetic long-context prompts and KV-caching enabled.

Immediate actions taken by ops (already applied):
- Rollback kernel to v1.3.0 for Halo4B (reverted the kernel flag) — stopped the majority of new 502s.
- Provisioned +2 nodes to the Halo4B pool to clear backlog and reduce contention.
- Forced fallback routing for long-context requests to halo4b-stable-quant (compatible but slightly higher latency).

Customer message suggestion (you can paste this):
"We identified a regression introduced by a recent kernel runtime change for Halo4B that affected requests with long context. We reverted the change and provisioned additional capacity; error rates are back to baseline for your traffic. We will follow up with a full postmortem and remediation plan within 72 hours."

Follow-ups / next work:
- Run full regression tests across sequence-length distributions and enable additional guard rails in kernel selection. (Owner: sergio)
- Add automated synthetic load that covers the long-context paths to our Canary harness. (Owner: hannah)
- Postmortem doc and remediation plan (owner: sergio) — aim to publish within 72 hours.

Attachments: mitigation-checklist.pdf includes the rollback steps and verification checklist.

Sergio

Subject: Halo4B elevated 502s — recovery confirmed and next steps

Hi Maya — quick update, and thank you for bearing with us.

Status: Full recovery confirmed at ~13:20 PST. Error rate for Halo4B traffic has returned to baseline (<0.2%) and streaming completions are stable.

What happened (short summary):
- A kernel selection regression (v1.3.2) for Halo4B did not correctly handle KV-cache pointer updates at certain sequence-length boundaries. The faulty code path could cause a streaming RPC to terminate with a 502.
- We reverted the kernel change (back to v1.3.0), provisioned extra capacity to clear the backlog, and applied a temporary routing policy to route long-context requests to halo4b-stable-quant during verification.

Customer impact and data safety:
- We did not detect cross-tenant cache leakage; requests stayed within tenant isolation boundaries. We will include sanitized verification logs in the postmortem.

Remediation and timeline:
- Postmortem (JIRA-INC-5427) will be published by Tue, 2026-11-17. It will include a root cause analysis, test coverage improvements, and an action list for a safer kernel rollout process.
- Short-term product changes: add sequence-length guard in kernel selector, expand canary coverage, and add synthetic long-context checks to CI. (Owners: Sergio / Hannah)
- We will offer a one-time service credit for the period of elevated errors; I’ll follow up with your billing contact to agree on amount.

Attachments: halo4b-error-samples.txt (truncated), request-ids.csv, mitigation-checklist.pdf

If you want a short call to walk through the postmortem when it is available, I’m happy to schedule one — otherwise we’ll send the doc and the log verification bundle.

Thanks again for your patience.

Best,
